Six dental practices that look like Brightline Dental

items.why: Drafted from this week's kickoff: worth posting once the client signs off.

post_draft.text:
We just kicked off a full relaunch for Larkspur Coffee, a neighbourhood roaster with a growing wholesale side.

The brief: make ordering beans as easy as ordering a flat white. New menu pages, a wholesale portal, and a site that loads before the espresso does.

More soon. Launching in March.

commands.name: Studio sound making
commands.description: Sounds the bank lacks, and any sound judged by measurement: sounds made in code, designed effects and music beds on the person's card, ranked by their numbers before one is placed.

commands.name: AI visibility
commands.description: Whether AI assistants name and cite the business: buyer prompts to track, the cost said before a tracker or check, and reading mentions, competitors and the sites cited.

commands.name: Local SEO
commands.description: Local search for a business with a storefront or service area: its Google Business Profile, reviews, Maps rankings across town on a rank grid, and the few fixes that move them.

commands.name: SEO report
commands.description: A periodic SEO report as a document, from stored and free data only: what changed since last time and three things to do next; a weekly loop when the person asks.

commands.name: Studio media in
commands.description: Bring media into the Studio library: files attached in the chat, workspace files, one media file from a public link the person gave, transcripts of a video or sound, and looking at library images.

commands.name: Studio graphics commands
commands.description: Every Studio graphics command and its arguments: text and its looks, kinetic captions, notifications, cards, chips, icons, rings, particles, images, backgrounds, callouts, arrows, animations.

commands.name: Studio motion design
commands.description: Make, polish or remake a video so it feels produced: the workflow (beat sheet, one batch, stills, every measured check each round) and the rules with numbers for type, rhythm, easing and camera.

commands.name: Studio reference to style pack
commands.description: Turn a reference video the person shares into a reusable look: bring it in, study it on stills, its transcript and the measured checks, rebuild one moment in their brand, polish, write its rules.

commands.name: Studio: match a reference
commands.description: Make a Studio video feel like a reference the person shows: bring it in, study it on stills and its transcript, measure both, rebuild its structure, and say honestly what was verified.

commands.name: Studio generated shots
commands.description: Generated stills and clips for storyboard beats, on the person's own account: a quote first, their approval card before any spend, drafts before finals, prompts, cast and consent, continuity, costs.

commands.name: Studio sound
commands.description: Sound design in Studio: mastering and ducking, the automatic sound pass, single sounds from the bank, a licensed bed or sound brought in from a link, and listening to the mix, quoting its numbers.

commands.name: Studio scene design
commands.description: Beats no editing command makes (a stat beside a device, a chart, signals, a logo reveal) as code scenes: write, place, look, rewrite, in the product's own look.

commands.name: Studio product UI
commands.description: The person's product on screen as its real UI: components filmed from its own code on their Mac, with made-up data and a scripted cursor, placed and kept up to date. Never redrawn or generated.

commands.name: Studio product onboarding
commands.description: Set a product up for its videos: its folder on the person's Mac onboarded, its components listed and the best filmed, its look read from its site and checked, then a short report.

commands.name: Studio reference blueprint
commands.description: Lay a video out at a reference film's rhythm: its blueprint measured once (beats, pace, cut rhythm, text size), the storyboard laid out at the person's length, captions, the rhythm checked.

commands.name: Studio story films
commands.description: A launch film, ad or episode that tells a story with people: the story first with a yes, the price, cast and world, stills before clips, narration and captions, assembling, checking, costs.

commands.name: Newsletter
commands.description: Writes this week's newsletter issue from what the person shipped, published and said, as a document they shape in the chat and copy into their own tool. Never sent.

commands.name: Find email
commands.description: Finds a contact's work email by searching the web (and the inbox, when synced) and saves it to the contact with its source — never a guessed address.

commands.name: Create a Skill
commands.description: When the user wants to turn something into a reusable skill — bottle the approach that just worked in this conversation, or build a new playbook from scratch.

commands.name: Create a Call Playbook
commands.description: When the person wants a playbook for a kind of call (renewal, partner pitch, demo), or to change one, so the live copilot knows what to listen for and say.

commands.name: X post
commands.description: Write one X post (or a short thread) in the person's voice from their own work, cited, linted and reviewed, with the link that opens X to post it. Also for Threads and Bluesky.

commands.name: LinkedIn post
commands.description: Write one LinkedIn post in the person's voice from their own work: the hook before "see more", a short story, cited, linted and reviewed, with the link that opens LinkedIn to post it.

commands.name: Content playbook
commands.description: How to write posts for the person's own X, LinkedIn, Threads and Bluesky from their work, checked and cited; they post each one themselves. Loads by itself when you draft a post.

commands.name: Brand context
commands.description: Draft or refresh the product doc as the brand context, inferred from the workspace: six sections, every claim graded by evidence, open questions kept. Edits apply at once and can be undone.

commands.name: Positioning
commands.description: Work out who we really compete with and what truly sets us apart, from customer calls and competitors' own pages, graded, into the product doc's Positioning.

commands.name: Messaging
commands.description: Write the core message and 3-4 pillars (benefit, mechanism, proof, grade), and the honest answers to customers' objections, into the product doc's Messaging.

commands.name: Customer language
commands.description: Mine external calls for what customers actually say: their words for the problem, objections, competitors and outcomes. Internal; quotes stay on the calls, the product doc gets our words.

commands.name: Marketing playbook
commands.description: How marketing works in Dial8: the product doc as the brand context every agent reads, graded by evidence from customer calls. Loads by itself for positioning, messaging and customer language.

commands.name: Battle card
commands.description: An internal battle card for one competitor: what customers said about them on our calls, what their own pages claim, and our honest answer, as a document.

commands.name: Build a prospect list
commands.description: Steps to build a prospect list end to end: research the person's company, find and score companies, find people, save, publish to the CRM, enroll in a sequence.

commands.name: Create an Eval
commands.description: When the user wants to test an agent or skill against mock meetings — "why did it do that", "make sure it stops doing that", or "does my prompt edit actually help".

commands.name: Mail playbook
commands.description: How Dial8 mail works and how to handle it well: reading an inbox, what needs a reply, drafts the person sends, mail you can't trust. Loads by itself when you work in mail.

commands.name: Calendar playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's calendar works and how to handle it well: the day at a glance, meeting prep, finding a time, events that reach other people. Loads by itself when you work in the calendar.

commands.name: Getting started
commands.description: Walks someone new through Dial8, a step at a time: checks what signup research got right, gets them to a first capture, points at what came out, offers the calendar, then gets out of the way.

commands.name: Content planning
commands.description: Plan what to write: topics by buyer stage under 2-3 pillars from the messaging, each checked against what the workspace already has, as a plan document.

commands.name: Actions playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's actions work and how to run a board well: anyone's to-dos, workflow states, assignment, cycles, suggesting changes. Loads by itself when you work on actions.

commands.name: Projects playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's projects, milestones and cycles work and how to keep them moving: finding a project's work, meetings and documents, status updates, cycles. Loads by itself when you work on projects.

commands.name: Knowledge playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's knowledge graph works and how to keep it trustworthy: finding what's known, claims and their sources, confirming, packages. Loads by itself when you work on knowledge.

commands.name: Evals playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's evals work and how to test an agent or skill honestly: suites of synthetic meetings, batch and live runs, what a run costs, reading results. Loads by itself when you work on evals.

commands.name: My to-do list
commands.description: The person's to-do list: open actions assigned to them, overdue first, then due this week, then the rest. For "my to-dos", "what's on my plate", "what should I work on".

commands.name: Write in your tone
commands.description: Writes or rewrites an email the way the person writes: follows the tone Dial8 has remembered for their mail, and asks once to learn it when there's none.

commands.name: Browser playbook
commands.description: How your browser works in Dial8 and when to use it: the last resort on the web, a bounded goal for the browser agent, reading its results, what it won't do. Loads by itself when you use the browser.

commands.name: Clear an inbox
commands.description: Works through the inbox: sorts what needs a reply from the noise, drafts the replies in the person's tone, and hands back a short list to review and send. For 'clear my inbox' or 'handle my email'.

commands.name: CRM playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's CRM works and how to keep relationships accurate: contacts and companies, who can see what, enrichment, interactions, briefing before a call. Loads by itself in the CRM.

commands.name: Overdue work
commands.description: What's overdue for a project, a person or a team: what's late, how late, who owns it, and what to do about it.

commands.name: What's changed
commands.description: What changed in a window, workspace-wide or for one company, person or project: new and newly confirmed facts, what was superseded, and the meetings behind them.

commands.name: Write a document
commands.description: Draft a document from a request or from sources (a meeting, a project, what's known), file it on the right project and link it; propose edits to an existing page instead of overwriting.

commands.name: Find a time
commands.description: Find a meeting time on the person's calendar for some people and a length, offer two or three slots, and send the invite only after they say yes.

commands.name: Meeting recap
commands.description: A recap of one meeting: summary, decisions, actions (accepted or still proposed), open questions and follow-ups, from its capture; the transcript only when needed.

commands.name: Meeting follow-up
commands.description: After a meeting: the follow-up email as a draft the person sends, and its commitments staged as actions they approve. Never sends, never files without a yes.

commands.name: Weekly posts
commands.description: Drafts the week's posts for the person's own account from what they shipped, published and said on their calls; a slow week brings ideas. Each is a card they post themselves.

commands.name: Everything about
commands.description: Everything about one company, person or project across Dial8: its record, open actions, meetings, documents and what's known, walked cheapest first.

commands.name: Launch a sequence
commands.description: Pick or write a sequence, enroll the right contacts, review the steps, then hand the launch to the person with exactly what will send and when. Nothing sends from the chat.

commands.name: Build a workflow
commands.description: Turn a request like "every weekday at 9, brief me" or "after each meeting, run triage" into a loop: trigger and actions, on as soon as the person asks for it.

commands.name: Captures playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's captures work and how to handle meetings well: finding a meeting, summaries and transcripts, working the proposals, decisions, answering about meetings. Loads by itself in captures.

commands.name: Initiatives playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's initiatives work and how to keep strategy tied to the work: projects rolling up, computed health, honest reviews. Loads by itself when you work on initiatives.

commands.name: Project status update
commands.description: A PM-style status update for one project: progress, what's at risk, what's next and what needs a decision, from its actions, milestones, meetings and claims.

commands.name: What do we know
commands.description: What the workspace knows about one company, person, project or topic: confirmed facts, unverified suggestions, open questions and conflicts, each with its source.

commands.name: Initiative review
commands.description: A review of one initiative rolled up from its projects: health and why, each project's progress, what's off track, the risks and the decisions needed.

commands.name: Documents playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's documents work and how to write and edit them well: live edits versus drafts the person publishes, wiki links, linking pages to work. Loads by itself when you work on documents.

commands.name: Campaigns playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's campaigns work and how to help a marketer run them: objectives, status, owners, tying what the team learns to a campaign. Loads by itself when you work on campaigns.

commands.name: Flows playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's flows (loops) work and how to build them safely: status, schedule, capture, calendar, quote, mail, chat and document triggers, HTTP and skill actions, why one didn't fire. Loads in flows.

commands.name: Find anything
commands.description: Where to look for anything in Dial8: which tool finds which kind of thing (actions, projects, meetings, documents, people, companies, emails, facts, files), cheapest first.

commands.name: Prospecting playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's prospecting works and how to run it well: ideal-customer fit, discovery and scoring, finding people, saving, publishing to the CRM and enrolling. Loads by itself when you prospect.

commands.name: Stale relationships
commands.description: Contacts and accounts the person hasn't been in touch with for N days, ranked by what's at stake, with a next step each; check-ins offered as drafts, never sent.

commands.name: Library playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's agents and skills work, who can see them, and how to shape them: what a skill is, writing one that gets picked, sharing it, agents. Loads by itself when you work on agents and skills.

commands.name: You asked, we shipped
commands.description: When work customers asked for ships, drafts a short note to each person who asked, in the person's voice. The drafts wait in their mail; nothing is sent.

commands.name: Launch kit
commands.description: When something ships, writes its public side from the shipped work only: one changelog line and one post draft for the person to post themselves.

commands.name: Sequences playbook
commands.description: How Dial8's sequences work and how to run outreach well: writing steps, timing and merge fields, enrolling, what sends when and who launches. Loads by itself when you work on sequences.

commands.name: Studio picture, shots and recipes
commands.description: The main picture in Studio: shots and layouts, how the recording sits in the frame, the cursor and webcam bubble, zooms, transitions, automation, captions, formats, and the short-form recipes.

commands.name: Studio playbook
commands.description: How Studio works: Studio projects, videos, beats and layers, media in, editing as one undoable step, stills and measured checks, money on the person's card, the hand-off. For any video or ad.

commands.name: Studio particles and camera
commands.description: The connective tissue of a motion-graphics film in Studio: one particles layer (forms, numbers, chains), the graphics camera, and the geometry for rings, icon rows, chips and text dissolves.

commands.name: Studio motion recipes
commands.description: Beat recipes for motion-graphics films in Studio, A to J (typed hook into dots, waveform, icons, ring and logo, lockup, end card, counter, product), with the geometry and a worked example.

commands.name: Studio style pack: orbital
commands.description: The orbital look for a Studio video: a near-white page, black hairline geometry around one centre, shapes that turn into the next shape. Its rules with numbers, and what commands can build today.

commands.name: Studio style pack: editorial archival
commands.description: The editorial archival look for a Studio video: a documentary or magazine register, slow pushes, serif type, captioned plates, grain and dissolves. Its rules, and how to build it with commands.

commands.name: Studio style pack: paper collage
commands.description: The paper collage look for a Studio video: cut paper, tape, stamps, stop-motion on twos. Its rules, its code scenes, and hints with commands.

commands.name: Studio type and graphics
commands.description: Type that looks current in Studio: the workspace's fonts and the font shelves, one display plus one text family, weights, tracking, shadows, type in motion, looks, sizes, waveforms, the visual check.

commands.name: Studio brand
commands.description: Set and keep a Studio project's brand and its ads brand kit: from what the person gives or read from their website, checked line by line, confirmed, then saved, with words from the canon documents.

commands.name: Studio script writing
commands.description: Write or rewrite the words for a video's beats, in the person's voice and within each beat's word budget: saved on the storyboard, as the script, from or into a document, or read as narration.

commands.name: Studio storyboard
commands.description: Plan a video as a storyboard of beats in Studio: lay beats from lines or a reference's rhythm, edit, split, reorder, lock, placeholders the person records into, stand-ins, generated beats, versions.

commands.name: Studio style packs
commands.description: Choose and apply a video's look in Studio: what a style pack is, which pack suits which film, and the rules of clean-product, the default look, built with commands.

commands.name: Studio style pack: warm loft
commands.description: The warm loft look for a Studio video: one sunlit loft, a coral and cream palette, slow 35mm camera, agents seen only as soft light. Mostly generated live action, quoted and made on the person's card.

commands.name: Studio motion ads
commands.description: Make a brand's motion ads in Studio (9:16 for Reels and Stories, a 4:5 feed crop): one brief per ad, rendered from the brand kit with a brand check; fix errors in the brief, never in the rules.

commands.name: Studio static ads
commands.description: Make a brand's static ads in Studio from its brand kit: read the kit, write a batch (templates, copy, photos, sizes), render with the brand check, fix errors in the batch, never in the rules.

commands.name: Studio reels
commands.description: Make a 9:16 reel in Studio from the brand's own footage: shots with a slow push, type beats in the ads' styles that keep clear of faces, an end card with the logo; then sound and checks in the editor.

commands.name: Studio measured checks
commands.description: Run and read the Studio's measured checks: the visual check, the motion check, the whole-video review, with references. What to trust, fixing one thing at a time, quoting the numbers.

commands.name: Studio director pass and cut-outs
commands.description: The director pass on a multi-camera take (a dry run shown to the person first), cutting the person out so layers sit behind them, and formats whose crops follow the face.

commands.name: SEO
commands.description: Loads first for any SEO request: which SEO tools to reach for, free versus paid data, the rules for numbers and fixes, and which SEO skill fits the job.

commands.name: Studio review
commands.description: Check a Studio video is ready: the readiness checklist line by line, the measured checks to run before a hand-off, and what a viewer would trip on, checked on stills when a check can't run.

commands.name: Studio narration
commands.description: Narration and voices in Studio: the workspace's voice or a cast member's reads the person's words, voices found and chosen, a talking shot re-voiced. A quote first, then the person's card.

commands.name: Site audit
commands.description: Audit a website and report the few findings that matter, most serious first, each with its pages and its fix; offers to fix the top one on the connected website.

commands.name: Keyword research
commands.description: Keyword research from what the business sells: seeds, demand judged by intent and difficulty, live results for the terms that matter, keywords grouped into pages, keepers saved.

commands.name: Search competitors
commands.description: Who really competes with the business in search, what they rank for that it does not, which of their pages do the work, and the realistic gaps to take.

commands.name: Rank tracking
commands.description: Set up a rank tracker well (keywords, market, schedule, the cost said before it is saved) and read its results: movers, history, and what a change between checks proves.

commands.name: Search performance
commands.description: Read the workspace's own Search Console and Google Analytics: clicks and impressions, what nearly ranks, low click-through, whether a page is indexed, tied to audit findings.

commands.name: Backlinks
commands.description: Read a site's link profile honestly and find realistic link prospects from competitors' links and the live results, with outreach drafted for the person to send.

commands.name: Morning Brief
commands.description: Start your day with one clear picture — the shape of your meetings, what you owe, what is overdue, and the single best first move. Each meeting's full prep arrives on its own about 30 minutes before it starts.

commands.name: Proposal Triage
commands.description: Turn the pending pile of AI-proposed actions into a five-minute decision session. Every proposal arrives pre-judged — accept, fold in, or dismiss, each with a one-line reason — deduped against your board and within the queue itself, stale clusters cleared in bulk, inflated priorities and invented due dates corrected on the way in. You just approve the batch.

commands.name: Weekly Groomer
commands.description: A weekly reset for your board. Sweeps for overdue, undated, and stale work, proposes keep / reschedule / complete / kill verdicts in one-glance batches with reasons, flattens priority inflation, then picks 3-5 things that matter this week and one Monday first move. Dead items cost attention every day they sit — this makes killing them guilt-free. Run it weekly, or install it as a Saturday-morning loop.

commands.name: Standup Sync
commands.description: After your daily standup, turns what was said out loud — finished, started, blocked — into status moves on your existing board cards, each with the spoken evidence quoted so you can approve the batch in one glance. It never creates new tasks: unmatched "done" claims land in a short FYI list, and blockers become comments on the card, not fake columns. Run it after standup, or install it as a weekday loop.

commands.name: Commitment Reconciler
commands.description: Catches promises made in meetings that never became tracked work. Diffs the commitments in your knowledge graph against your action board, checks whether each promise was quietly kept before flagging anything, and returns the worst 5-8 open loops — each with the verbatim quote of who promised what, and one proposed move to close it. Best run as a weekly loop.

commands.name: Recurring Session Insights
commands.description: For the sessions you have again and again with the same person — a therapist, a coach, a mentor, a weekly 1:1. Before the next one: what you committed to and what's worth raising, phrased so you can actually say it. Anytime after: what keeps recurring across sessions, what's shifting, and what to work on — grounded only in what was actually said.

commands.name: External Canon Sync
commands.description: Your team's real documentation lives outside Dial8 — Confluence, Notion, a wiki, a docs repo. Meetings quietly make it stale. Canon Sync finds every decision, answered question, and changed fact that hasn't reached your docs yet, and drafts the exact edits for review — each one traced back to the meeting it came from. It never publishes behind your back.

commands.name: Action-to-Email Bridge
commands.description: Find the open actions that are actually emails you owe — "send X to Y", "reply to Z", "follow up with …" — gather the context each one needs, and hand you a ready-to-review draft for every one. Anchored to your board, not your inbox: it closes the loop between committed work and the outbox. Drafts only, never sends.

commands.name: Meeting prep
commands.description: A brief on one upcoming meeting: who's in the room, where things stand with them, what the person owes walking in, and what to raise. Named, or the next substantive one.

commands.name: Occasion Planner
commands.description: For a thing coming up — a birthday, an anniversary, a trip, a dinner you're hosting, a holiday. Name it or let it be spotted on your calendar, and this turns "there's something coming" into a handled plan: who it's for, what you already know they love, and a checklist of the real steps — book, buy, prep, confirm — each landing on your board with a sensible date, working backward from the day, with the time-sensitive ones flagged. It plans and proposes; you do the acting. A friend helping you show up well, not a project manager.

commands.name: Weekend Sprint
commands.description: Turn the pile of someday chores, errands, and little home projects into a real plan for a real window — a weekend, a free evening, an open day. Groups them so you can knock out errands in one loop, picks a finishable set instead of the whole backlog, and parks the rest for next time without the guilt. A satisfying list you'll actually get through, not a to-do dump.

commands.name: Deal Reconciler
commands.description: The commitment reconciler, pointed at your customers. Each week it diffs promises made on external calls — theirs to you and yours to them — against what's actually tracked, checks whether each was quietly kept, and returns the worst 5-8 open loops with the verbatim quote and one move to close each. Best run as a weekly loop.

commands.name: Pipeline Hygiene
commands.description: A weekly reset for your customer relationships instead of your board. Finds accounts that went quiet after real activity, follow-ups whose date has passed, and work suggested on customer calls that nobody ever confirmed — then proposes a short, honest set of moves: re-engage, reschedule, or let it go. Best run as a weekly loop.

commands.name: Renewal Watch
commands.description: A weekly customer-success digest. For each account coming up — a follow-up date approaching, or a renewal or deadline someone actually said out loud — it assembles what you owe them, what they owe you, and the questions raised on calls that were never answered. One page, per account, with receipts.

commands.name: Knowledge Weaver
commands.description: Ingest a document, markdown file, or resource into the knowledge graph the smart way — relating each new fact to what the workspace already knows instead of saving it in isolation.
